thread:
maria: Quick follow-up from the atomic-load-fallback operator RFC. We circled on two mutually exclusive approaches: block inference until full shard is verified vs return a partial tensor and mark it as 'repairable'. I sketched a minimal operator API and a fallback policy. Would like quick sanity-check before I add this to the loader refactor PR.

aj: Short thought — leaning toward non-blocking partial loads for latency reasons. But we need strong invariants so operators don't return silently corrupted activations.

maria: Agreed. Proposal: operator returns (tensor_handle, validity_mask, status). status can be one of {ok, partial_repair_scheduled, fatal}. validity_mask is per-chunk bitmask, not per-byte. Repair runs async and can update a KV with repaired chunk checksums.

leo: How does this interact with safetensors and sharded checkpoints? safetensors is slice-friendly, but there is no standard chunk-checksum today. We should avoid inventing heavyweight crypto here.

maria: Right — prefer lightweight checksums (crc32) per chunk in a small sidecar manifest. Matching chunk sizes to the store transfer block helps. If no manifest present, operator falls back to conservative "fatal" for that shard (unless config allows partial_ok).

aj: Can we show the config example? small snippet pls.

maria: Sure — drafted config snippet: 
```json
{
  "atomic_load_fallback": {
    "fallback_strategy": "stream-merge", // options: stream-merge | block-until-verified | zero-fill
    "repair_window_s": 60,
    "max_read_retry": 2,
    "allow_partial_by_default": false
  }
}
```

sylvia: stream-merge = return partial + stream repaired bytes in-place when ready? That sounds fancy but also race-prone. How do callers observe an in-place repair vs new allocation?

maria: Implementation plan: tensor_handle is a thin indirection to an underlying buffer. validity_mask lets runtime know which KV-cache entries are missing. When repair completes, we either fill the buffer in-place (if supported) or swap to a repaired buffer and publish a short "repair-complete" trace so tracing/console can reconcile. We must expose an api on the handle: handle.wait_for_repair(timeout_s) for callers that need consistency.

leo: Edge-case: quantized tensors where a partial fill will blow numeric stability on layernorm. For these models I'd prefer block-until-verified by default. We could add a model-level annotation in the manifest: "atomic_preference": "no-partial" so serving/runtime can override.

aj: Ops concerns: how does this affect OOM and eviction? If we keep partials around we need to track approximate memory used and evict properly. Also repair storms if many replicas attempt repair at once. Suggest we add a repair leader election per-shard (ttl lease) and backoff jitter.

maria: Good call. Add to config: leader_ttl_s, repair_jitter_ms, and a per-shard repair-rate limit. Also emit telemetry: repair_attempt, repair_succeeded, repair_failed.

ops-bot: Deploy note: canary rollout of the loader-refactor (w/fallback operator) scheduled for 2026-04-03 02:00 UTC to us-west-2.

sylvia: Sounds good. Action items I can take: 1) add manifest schema with per-chunk crc32 + atomic_preference, 2) add handle.wait_for_repair API and doc snippets, 3) add leader election sketch for repair. I can start a PR for the manifest schema.

maria: Awesome — sylvia please add a short compatibility table for existing safetensors bundles (i.e., what happens if manifest missing). I'll update the RFC doc and the loader-refactor branch with the operator shim. Thanks all :thumbsup:

leo: One more: add a lightweight test harness that simulates mid-read failure and validates correctness under stream-merge and block modes. I can take that.

maria: Perfect. If nobody objects I'll push the loader shim and wire the config defaults as discussed. If something pops up, flag it here and we can pause the canary. :eyes:
